models_evaluated: CNN ensemble with XGBoost meta-learner (VHD and cardiomyopathy AI-ECG models)

links.outcome: External validation AUROC of hospital-trained AI-ECG models in athlete screening population versus internal validation
links.effect: AUROC fell to 0.70 (95% CI 0.64-0.75) for VHD and 0.69 (95% CI 0.60-0.78) for CM; NPV ~99%, PPV ≤8%.
links.quote: External validation demonstrated substantial performance degradation compared with hospital-based internal validation.

links.outcome: Performance transportability from hospital development population to low-prevalence athlete screening population
links.effect: Substantial degradation on external validation; AUROC 0.70 for VHD and 0.69 for CM; PPV ≤8% reflecting limited disease enrichment and prevalence dependence.
links.quote: Hospital-trained AI-ECG models demonstrated limited transportability to real-world athlete screening populations.

links.outcome: Predictive values at local screening prevalence versus hospital-based performance
links.effect: NPV ~99% but PPV ≤8% at low prevalence (VHD 4.3%, CM 2.7%), showing strong prevalence dependence.
links.quote: Threshold analyses showed high negative predictive values (∼99%) but persistently low positive predictive values (≤8%), reflecting limited disease enrichment and strong prevalence dependence.

screen.reason: Empirically tests the transportability/external validation of hospital-trained AI-ECG models to an athlete pre-participation screening cohort, demonstrating severe performance degradation and low PPV due to spectrum effects and prevalence differences.

primary.practice: external validation in target screening population
